:::{#def-expected-generalization-error}
#### Expected generalization error

A fitting procedure is a method
that turns any training set $\mathcal{T}$ into a prediction rule $\fitted$.
The **expected generalization error** of a fitting procedure
at training-set size $n$
is the mean of the [generalization error](#def-generalization-error)
of the rule it produces,
over training sets of $n$ observations
drawn independently from the population:

$$
\expgenerr{n} \eqdef \E{\generr_{\mathcal{T}}},
\quad
\mathcal{T} = \set{(X_1, Y_1), \ldots, (X_n, Y_n)}.
$$ {#eq-expected-generalization-error}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

@hastie2009elements [sec. 7.2] call this quantity the *expected prediction error*
(or *expected test error*) and write it $\generr$;
the argument $n$ is added here
because cross-validation fits rules to training sets smaller than $n$.
:::

:::
